newsitem.title: UK: Slovenia's debut mark bond spread tightens-dealers.
newsitem.headline: Slovenia's debut mark bond spread tightens-dealers.

text.p: Slovenia's first mark bond, launched Tuesday, performed well and was priced competitively, a syndicate source close to the deal said.
"Given that it is pretty tight pricing it has performed exceptionally well," he said.
The 300 million mark seven-year bond was priced to yield 43 basis points over the 6.75 percent Treuhand.
Joint lead managers for the transaction were CSFB and Dresdner Kleinwort Benson.
The syndicate source said the spread had tightened to trade around 41 b.p. bid over.
"We managed to capture a lot of institutional demand, and our key aim was to diversify the investor base," he said. "We have sold out of our allocation."
He said a lot of investors who were unable to participate in Slovenia's successful dollar transaction were now able to buy the mark bond.
The Republic of Slovenia is rated A3 by Moody's Investors Service and A by Standard and Poor's Corp.

Slovenian Finance Minister Mitja Gaspari recently said the deal was a strategic transaction not an opportunistic one and the proceeds would be used to retire, restructure and replace the country's debt.

Last July, Slovenia launched a debut Eurobond issue via J.P. Morgan. The $325 million five-year deal was priced to yield 58 basis points over U.S. Treasury notes, at the time the tightest spread for any Eurobond out of Eastern Europe. The deal has tightened around 10 b.p. in secondary market trade.
Gaspari also said Slovenia will launch a syndicate loan in either dollars or marks in late October and a Samurai bond early next year.
